A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fatigue strength of a welded joint is not only dependent on the initial residual stresses, but also on their variation under fatigue loading, which is mainly controlled by the weld geometry.
the fatigue strength of a welded joint is a function of its global geometry, its local geometry, the residual stress state and the load history.
the fatigue strength of a welded joint can be estimated from a single value of the notch stress intensity factor, provided that the effect of residual stresses is taken into account.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fatigue life of welded joints can be accurately predicted by means of a simple model based on a few input parameters.
the fatigue strength of a welded joint is sensitive to residual stresses even for high-cycle loading.
the effect of fatigue on the residual stress redistribution near weld toe can be quantified by the ratio of the NSIF due to residual stresses to that due to the nominal applied stress.
